name: Samsung Galaxy S9
summary: ztOS's first phone, and the reference port. Mainline Linux 7.1 with the Exynos 9810 drivers, booting from the phone's internal storage, with TWRP left in RECOVERY. Runs ztOS daily.
specs: 4× Mongoose M3 at 2.7 GHz, 4× Cortex-A55 at 1.8 GHz
Mainline Linux 7.1, modules for the phone's hardware

install.markdown:
> **This erases the phone.** Android and everything in its storage are replaced. The IMEI and modem calibration (EFS) are never touched, and the stock Android partitions stay, because the modem needs them.
>
> **Only the Exynos Galaxy S9 works:** SM-G960F or SM-G960N (`starlte`). The US Snapdragon S9 (SM-G960U) does not.

## What you need

- A Linux computer (x86-64 or ARM) with **15 GB free** and an internet connection
- A USB-C **data** cable (some only charge)
- The phone charged above **50%**
- About **2 hours**, mostly waiting

## 1. Install the tools on your computer

Arch Linux:

```sh
sudo pacman -S --needed git util-linux libarchive dosfstools mtools e2fsprogs \
    qemu-user-static qemu-user-static-binfmt android-tools heimdall socat
```

Debian / Ubuntu (not yet tested):

```sh
sudo apt install git uidmap libarchive-tools dosfstools mtools e2fsprogs \
    qemu-user-static binfmt-support adb heimdall-flash socat
```

The build runs as you, without `sudo`, so your account needs a range of user IDs. Check:

```sh
grep $USER /etc/subuid
```

If that prints nothing, add one, then **log out and back in**:

```sh
sudo usermod --add-subuids 100000-165535 --add-subgids 100000-165535 $USER
```

## 2. Get ztOS

```sh
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Zerone-Laboratories/ztOS.git
cd ztOS
installer/ztos doctor
```

`doctor` should end with **this computer can build ztOS**. Install anything it says is missing, then run it again.

## 3. Unlock the bootloader

1. Back up the phone. Unlocking erases it.
2. In Android: **Settings > About phone > Software information**, tap **Build number** seven times.
3. **Settings > Developer options > OEM unlocking**: on.
   No such switch? Connect to Wi-Fi and wait: Samsung shows it up to 7 days after setup.
4. Turn the phone off. Hold **Volume Down + Bixby** and plug in the USB cable.
5. On the warning screen, **long-press Volume Up** to unlock. The phone erases itself and restarts.
6. Go through Android's setup quickly, and check **OEM unlocking** is still on.

## 4. Put TWRP in RECOVERY

Download the TWRP image for the Galaxy S9 (`starlte`) from [twrp.me](https://twrp.me/samsung/samsunggalaxys9.html), and save it as `twrp-starlte.img`.

1. Turn the phone off. Hold **Volume Down + Bixby + Power**, then press **Volume Up** for download mode.
2. On the computer:

   ```sh
   heimdall flash --RECOVERY twrp-starlte.img --no-reboot
   ```

   (On Windows, Odin: TWRP in the **AP** slot, **Auto Reboot** off.)
3. Hold **Volume Down + Power** to leave download mode, and **the moment the screen goes black**, switch to **Volume Up + Bixby + Power**. If Android starts instead, it puts its own recovery back: repeat this step.
4. In TWRP, swipe to allow changes.

## 5. Connect the phone in TWRP

Plug the phone in and check the computer sees it:

```sh
adb devices
```

You should see one device, as `recovery`. (Later, to start TWRP: power off, then hold **Volume Up + Bixby + Power**.)

## 6. Build and install ztOS

```sh
installer/ztos install --target starlte --mode build-install
```

It asks, in order:

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Go on? (after the phone guide) | `y` |
| user name | the name you'll log in with |
| password, then again | at least 4 characters; for logging in and `sudo` |
| the phone's name | anything, e.g. `ztos` |
| time zone | e.g. `Asia/Colombo` |
| Start? | `y` |

Then **wait 30 to 60 minutes** the first time while it builds the system. The S9's boot image comes ready-made from `prebuilts/boot/`.

When it asks:

1. **Write ztOS's boot image to BOOT?** Answer `y`. It is read back and checked.
2. **Type ERASE to go on.** Type `ERASE`. The phone restarts into ztOS's rescue shell, and the system is written over USB in checked 256 MiB pieces: **10 to 20 minutes**.

If the cable comes out or it stops, run the same `installer/ztos install` command again: it carries on where it stopped.

## 7. Start ztOS

When the installer says **done**, hold **Power + Volume Up + Volume Down** until the phone restarts.

The first start takes **about a minute** while the system grows to fill the storage. Then log in with your user and password, and the Welcome app shows how ztOS works. With internet, Android apps set themselves up in the background on the first start (Waydroid downloads about 1 GB once).

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What to do |
|---|---|
| `the phone is not in TWRP over adb` | Start TWRP (step 5), try another cable or USB port, then `adb devices` |
| It waits for the phone on `172.16.42.1` | The phone hands your computer `172.16.42.2` over USB. If `ip addr` doesn't show it, set that USB network connection to **automatic (DHCP)**, then run the install again |
| The phone is stuck in **ztOS Rescue** | `installer/ztos`, then choose **3** |
| The phone goes back to TWRP by itself | ztOS didn't start and fell back safely. Run the install again from step 5 |
| Back to Android | Flash Samsung's stock firmware for your model with Odin or Heimdall from download mode |

notes.title: The modem or sensor hub doesn't come up
notes.text: It tends to follow a forced reboot or a crash. One pass through TWRP brings them back: `systemctl reboot --reboot-argument=recovery`, then `adb shell reboot` once TWRP is up. A full power-off also works.

notes.title: A driver that crashed while loading is skipped at the next boot
notes.text: So a crash can't become a boot loop. Remove its mark file under `/var/lib` to try it again.

notes.title: Reboot rather than unload a driver
notes.text: A failed module unload has left the phone unable to shut down.

notes.title: Keep the stock Android partitions
notes.text: The installer writes only BOOT and USERDATA; the modem needs the rest.

notes.title: Getting back in
notes.text: If Arch doesn't come up, the initramfs opens a rescue shell on the USB network. If the kernel hangs, a watchdog resets the phone into TWRP after 30 seconds. Download mode, which can't be overwritten, can always put the stock firmware back.
